requirements.text: The business must maintain a register of business entities, the umbrella concept covering all customers, vendors and employees.
Each business entity must be identified by a single company-wide business entity number that is unique across every party, regardless of whether the party is a customer, vendor or employee.

The business entity number must be usable to link a party to information held in other business areas such as sales, purchasing and HR, with the party register acting as the integration point for the company.
requirements.obj: party to information in other business areas

requirements.text: The business must be able to recognise that the same party may play more than one role at the same time, for example an employee who is also a retail customer.
The system must not force a party into a single role.
Each business entity record must carry a last-changed timestamp recording when it was last updated, so the business can understand the currency of the party register.
Each business entity record carries a globally unique record identifier that exists to support data replication between systems.
The globally unique record identifier has no business meaning, is not a business key, must be treated as technical metadata and needs no business reporting.
The business must record every person it deals with, identified by the same company-wide business entity number as the business entity.
A person must not have a separate identifier of their own; every person is a business entity and uses the same party number.
The business must record the primary type of each person, which classifies why the person exists in the company's systems.
The recognised primary person types are store contact, individual (retail) customer, salesperson, employee (non-sales), vendor contact and general contact.
The business must be able to count, segment and filter people by their primary type in every analysis, for example the number of individual customers held in Germany.
The list of person types is a small, fixed set of codes held in the person record itself rather than in a separate reference list.
The warehouse must present the meaning of each person type code in business language rather than the two-letter code.
The business must record each person's first name, middle name or middle initial, and last name.
The business must record an optional courtesy title, such as Mr. or Ms., for use in correspondence.
The business must record an optional surname suffix, such as Sr. or Jr.
The business must record a name style indicating whether a person's name is presented in western order (first name then last name) or eastern order (last name then first name).
Any report or output that displays a person's full name must be able to honour the recorded name style and must not assume western ordering.
Middle name, title and suffix are optional, and reporting must cope with people who have none of them.
The business must record each person's email promotion preference, which expresses the consent given for marketing contact.
The recognised email promotion preference levels are: no email promotions, email promotions from AdventureWorks only, and email promotions from AdventureWorks and selected partners.
Marketing and campaign selection must be able to filter people by email promotion preference.
Marketing and campaign selection must be able to distinguish the company-only consent case from the company-and-partners consent case, because the two permit different uses of a person's details.

The business must be able to state what a person's email promotion preference was historically, not only the current value, so the warehouse must introduce historical tracking of consent changes if an audit trail is required.
Consent is a compliance-sensitive attribute.
The business must retain additional contact information held for a person in a free-form structured XML format.
The business must retain demographic information collected from online shoppers, such as hobbies and income, which is captured for sales analysis.
Demographic content must be made analysable, for example to segment customers by income band or interest, rather than stored as an opaque block.
Access to demographic and additional contact information must be treated as sensitive and restricted separately from ordinary name and contact reporting.
Each person record must carry a last-changed timestamp so the business can know how current a person's details are and identify records that have not been touched for a long time.
The business must record the email addresses of people.
A person may have more than one email address, each numbered within the person, and the business must be able to report all of a person's email addresses, not just one.
An email address belongs to exactly one person and is meaningless without that person.
The business must be able to identify people who have no email address, since they cannot be reached by email campaigns regardless of promotion preference.
Each email address must carry its own last-changed timestamp so the business can see when a person's email details were last touched independently of the rest of their record.

The business must be able to understand whether an email address currently on file is still the one previously used in a campaign, so the warehouse must retain superseded email addresses historically.
The business must record the telephone numbers of people.
A person may have several telephone numbers, and each number is qualified by its phone number type.
The business must maintain a reference list of phone number types, each with a name describing the kind of number, such as home, work or mobile.
Reporting must be able to select a person's telephone number by type, for example the work number of every store contact in Bavaria.
A telephone number belongs to exactly one person.
Each telephone number must carry its own last-changed timestamp.
The business needs consistent naming of phone number types over time, because renaming a type changes the meaning of historical reporting.
The business records a sign-in credential for a person, consisting of a protected (hashed) password value and the random value used to protect it.
Credentials must never be brought into the warehouse as readable values, reported on, or exposed to analysts.

The only business-relevant facts about a credential are whether a person has one and when it was last changed, indicating whether the person has a self-service account and how recently it was maintained.
The whole credential record should be excluded from scope if the business does not need to know whether a person has a credential and when it was last changed.
A credential is attached to a person by the same party number, and one person has at most one credential.
The business must record postal addresses, each identified by its own address number.
An address consists of a first street address line, an optional second street address line, a city, a postal code, and the state or province in which it sits.
The state or province determines the country, so the country of an address is known indirectly through its state or province rather than being stated on the address itself.

The business must record the geographic location (latitude and longitude) of an address to support mapping, distance and territory analysis, such as showing reseller stores on a map or measuring customer distance from a store.
Addresses must be reportable at each geographic level: street, city, postal code, state or province, and country or region.
Each address carries a last-changed timestamp so the business can see when address details were corrected.

An address is recorded once and can be shared by more than one party, such as several employees of the same reseller store or a household; the business must not assume an address belongs to a single party.

The business needs to decide whether historical address values must be retained so that past activity can be reported against the address as it stood at the time, since address records can be edited in place.
The business must record which addresses belong to which business entity, and in what capacity.
A party can have several addresses, and the same address can serve several parties.
Every party-address relationship must carry an address type stating the role the address plays for that party, such as Billing, Home or Shipping.
A party may have different addresses for different purposes, for example one address to bill and another to ship to.
The combination of party, address and address type makes a party-address relationship unique, so a party may hold the same address under two different types and both must be visible.
The business must maintain a reference list of address types, each with a descriptive name.
The business must be able to answer what the shipping address of a given customer is.
The business must be able to answer which customers ship to a given city.
Each party-address relationship carries its own last-changed timestamp.

If the business needs to know which address a party used at a given point in the past, the warehouse must build and keep the history of party-address relationships, because the source holds only the currently valid set.
The business must be able to identify parties with no address on file, since these cannot be shipped to or invoiced by post.
The business must maintain a reference list of countries and regions, each identified by its ISO standard country or region code and carrying its name.
The business must maintain a reference list of states and provinces, each identified by its own number and carrying an ISO standard state or province code and a descriptive name.
Every state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.
A country or region may contain many states or provinces, and some may contain none.
The system carries a flag on a state or province indicating that no genuine state or province code exists and the country or region code is used in its place.
Reporting must handle states or provinces flagged as having no genuine code gracefully and must not present a substituted country code as if it were a real state code.
requirements.obj: state or province with no genuine code

requirements.text: Every state or province is assigned to a sales territory, linking where an address is to the part of the sales organisation responsible for it.
The business must be able to roll addresses, and therefore customers, stores and employees, up to sales territory via their state or province, to support territory-level sales and coverage reporting.
The warehouse must obtain sales territory descriptions from the sales area, because only the assignment of a state or province to a territory is available in this area.
The business can change the territory assignment of a state or province, which retrospectively changes historical geographic roll-ups.
The business must decide whether territory assignments should be tracked over time so that past performance can be reported on the territory structure that applied at the time.
requirements.obj: tracking of territory assignments over time

requirements.text: Country, state and territory reference lists each carry a last-changed timestamp.
Consistent, current naming of countries and states or provinces is required for customer-facing output and reporting, and renames must be visible rather than silent.
The business must record which people act as contacts for which organisations, such as the named individual who is the contact at a reseller store or supplier.
A contact relationship links two parties: the organisation (a business entity) and the person acting as its contact.
Every contact relationship must carry a contact type describing the role the person plays for that organisation.
The business must maintain a reference list of contact types, each with a descriptive name.
The same organisation may have several contacts, each in a different role, and the combination of organisation, person and role makes the contact relationship unique.
The same person may act as a contact for more than one organisation and may hold more than one role at the same organisation.
The business must be able to answer who the contact is at a given store and in what role.
The business must be able to answer which organisations a given person represents.
Each contact relationship carries its own last-changed timestamp.

If the business needs to know who the contact was at a given time, such as when investigating a past order, the warehouse must retain the history of contact relationships, because the source holds only the current set.

Reporting must clearly distinguish which side of a contact relationship is the organisation and which is the individual, using the party's role, because the relationship itself does not label them and both sides use the same party number.
requirements.obj: organisation and individual in contact relationship

requirements.text: The business needs a single view of a party bringing together, for one party number, their name and type, all email addresses, all telephone numbers with types, all addresses with types, and all organisations they are a contact for.
Reporting must correctly reflect that email addresses, telephone numbers, addresses and contact relationships are one-to-many for a party, and must not assume a person has exactly one of each.
The single view of a party must remain correct when a party plays several roles at once.
Every record in this area carries only a last-modified timestamp, and the operational system holds current state only, overwriting previous values in place.

The business currently has no history for a person's name, marketing consent, email address, telephone numbers, address details, party-address usage, organisational contacts and roles, or state-to-territory assignment, all of which change and matter analytically.

The warehouse must preserve the full history of change for person names, marketing consent, email addresses, telephone numbers, address details, party-address relationships, contact relationships and state or province territory assignments, so past activity can be reported against the details that applied at the time.
The last-changed timestamp on each record is the only change signal the source provides, and its reliability must be confirmed with the operational system owners.

The source provides no deletion marker or status flag in this area, so removed parties, addresses or relationships simply disappear; the business must state whether removals need to be detected and retained.
The business needs visibility of incomplete party records: people without an email address, without a phone number, or without any address.

The business needs visibility of duplicate people, meaning the same individual registered more than once under different party numbers, because duplicates affect customer counts and campaign accuracy.
The business needs visibility of addresses whose geographic location is missing, since these cannot be mapped or measured for territory purposes.
Reporting should highlight states or provinces carrying the no-genuine-code flag rather than hide them, as they signal incomplete geographic reference data.
requirements.obj: states or provinces with no genuine code

requirements.text: Reference lists (address type, contact type, phone number type, country or region, state or province) must be complete so that every relationship and address resolves to a named type, country or region.
Unresolvable references to reference lists are a data quality defect and must be reported.

This area holds personal data about identifiable individuals, including names, home addresses, private email addresses, telephone numbers, geographic coordinates, marketing consent, and self-declared demographics including income.
Access to person-level detail must be restricted to roles with a legitimate business need.
Aggregated reporting, such as counts by region, person type and consent level, should be available more widely than person-level detail.
Sign-in credentials must be excluded from all analytical use.
Marketing consent must be respected by every downstream use of the data, including any extract that leaves the warehouse.
The distinction between consent for our company only and consent for our company and partners must be carried through to any sharing decision.
The business needs to be able to answer, for an individual, what personal data it holds about them across this area, supported by the single view of a party.
requirements.obj: personal data held about an individual

requirements.text: The company-wide party number is assumed to be stable and never re-used for a different party, which must be confirmed with the operational system owners.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 states each business entity is identified by a single company-wide number unique across all parties; REQ-003 uses it for integration and REQ-065 assumes it is stable and never re-used (to be confirmed). Satisfies uniqueness, stability and business recognition.

REQ-009 and REQ-010 state a person is identified by the same company-wide party number as the business entity and has no separate identifier. Unique, non-null, business-recognised; shares the key with business entity.
REQ-007 and REQ-008 explicitly say the globally unique record identifier exists for replication, has no business meaning and is not a business key. Technical metadata only.

REQ-001-2 states each postal address is identified by its own address number. It is the only identifier for an address in the requirements, though it is a system-style number and no natural alternative is given.

REQ-014-2 and REQ-011-2 describe a reference list of address types with descriptive names used to qualify party-address relationships (REQ-013-2). The identifier is not explicitly named, so confidence is moderate.
REQ-014-2 gives each address type a descriptive name such as Billing, Home or Shipping, which the business recognises. Name stability is at risk if types are renamed.
REQ-036-2 and REQ-035-2 describe a contact type reference list with descriptive names, used in the contact relationship uniqueness in REQ-037-2. The identifier is not explicitly stated.
REQ-036-2 gives each contact type a descriptive name recognised by the business. Renaming could affect stability.
REQ-040 and REQ-041 describe a reference list of phone number types qualifying each telephone number. The identifier is not explicitly called unique, so confidence is moderate.
REQ-041 gives each type a name such as home, work or mobile. REQ-045 warns that renaming changes the meaning of history, which undermines stability.
REQ-020-2 states each country or region is identified by its ISO standard code. It is a stable, unique, business-recognised standard code.
REQ-021-2 states each state or province is identified by its own number. It is unique and used by the business for the reference list, but it is an assigned number.
REQ-021-2 says states have an ISO standard code. REQ-024-2 and REQ-025-2 note some have no genuine code and a country code is substituted, so it is not reliably unique or non-null on its own.

REQ-034 says email addresses are numbered within the person, and REQ-035 says an address belongs to exactly one person and is meaningless without them. This composite of the party number and the sequence number identifies an email address, which is a dependent child of person.

REQ-039, REQ-040 and REQ-043 say a person has several telephone numbers, each qualified by a phone number type, and each number belongs to one person. The composite is inferred from the source columns and is not explicitly stated as the identifier.
REQ-013-2 explicitly states that the combination of party, address and address type makes a party-address relationship unique.
REQ-037-2 explicitly states that the combination of organisation, person and role makes the contact relationship unique. REQ-043-2 notes both sides use the same party number.
REQ-050 says a credential is attached to a person by the same party number and one person has at most one credential. Note REQ-047 and REQ-061 exclude credential values from analytical use.

schema.description: Unique identifier of the address record (business key).

schema.name: AddressLine1
schema.description: First line of the street address.

schema.name: AddressLine2
schema.description: Optional second line of the street address.

schema.name: City
schema.description: Name of the city of the address.

schema.name: StateProvinceID
schema.description: Identifier of the state or province of the address; references StateProvince.

schema.name: PostalCode
schema.description: Postal code of the address.

schema.name: SpatialLocation
schema.description: Geographic spatial location data for the address.

schema.name: rowguid

schema.name: ModifiedDate

contracts.name: AddressType
contracts.doc: Reference data describing the types of addresses (e.g. billing, shipping) that can be associated with a business entity, staged from the source AddressType table. The contract enforces the declared schema, key and not-null constraints; value-level semantics are left for producer/consumer negotiation.

schema.name: AddressTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the address type; business key of the AddressType asset.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the address type.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row, used by the source system for row identification and replication.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the row was last modified in the source system.

contracts.name: BusinessEntity
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset for BusinessEntity, the base record that identifies a business entity (such as a person) by BusinessEntityID. The contract enforces schema, primary key and not-null rules. Ownership and agreement are left to human-in-the-loop review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity. It is the business key of this asset.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the source row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: BusinessEntityAddress
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset for BusinessEntityAddress: associates a business entity with an address and the address type (role) it plays for that entity. The contract enforces the declared schema and the deterministic business-key, primary-key and not-null rules; ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (e.g. person, store, vendor) the address is linked to. Refers to BusinessEntity.BusinessEntityID.

schema.name: AddressID
schema.description: Identifier of the address linked to the business entity. Refers to Address.AddressID.

schema.name: AddressTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the type of address (role) for this business entity/address link. Refers to AddressType.AddressTypeID.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row, used by the source system for row identification.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: BusinessEntityContact
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset linking a business entity to a contact person and the type of contact relationship. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key integrity; value-level checks are limited to what is stated in requirements.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity that the contact relationship belongs to; references BusinessEntity.

schema.name: PersonID
schema.description: Identifier of the person who acts as the contact for the business entity; references Person.

schema.name: ContactTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the type of contact relationship; references ContactType.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) assigned in the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: ContactType
contracts.doc: Reference data describing the types of contact (e.g. roles) that a business entity contact can have. One record per contact type, identified by ContactTypeID. The contract enforces the declared schema, primary key and not-null rules; value-level constraints are left for producer/consumer negotiation.

schema.name: ContactTypeID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the contact type; the business key of this reference table.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the contact type.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the contact type record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: CountryRegion
contracts.doc: Reference data for countries/regions, sourced from the CountryRegion source table and landed in staging. The contract enforces the declared schema and the business key CountryRegionCode; value-level semantics are left for producer/consumer negotiation at the human review checkpoint.

schema.name: CountryRegionCode
schema.description: Code that identifies a country or region; the business key of the asset.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the country or region.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: EmailAddress
contracts.doc: Email addresses associated with a business entity (person) in the source-to-staging load of the EmailAddress source table. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key identity; value-level constraints are left for producer/consumer review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (person) that owns this email address; references BusinessEntity/Person.

schema.name: EmailAddressID
schema.description: Identifier of the email address row, distinguishing multiple email addresses for the same business entity.

schema.name: EmailAddress
schema.description: The email address text for the business entity.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the source row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: Password
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset for Password: stores credential material (hash and salt) associated with a business entity (person). The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key integrity; ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint. Contains sensitive credential fields that warrant review for handling/masking.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (person) to which this password record belongs; business key referencing BusinessEntity.

schema.name: PasswordHash
schema.description: Hashed representation of the password. Sensitive credential material.

schema.name: PasswordSalt
schema.description: Salt value used when hashing the password. Sensitive credential material.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Row-level globally unique identifier (GUID) for the record.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified.

contracts.name: Person
contracts.doc: Staging contract for the Person source table: one record per person (individual) associated with a business entity, including name parts, person type, and contact-preference attributes. Schema, primary-key and not-null breaches are enforced as hard failures by the core; no value-level constraints are mandated by the requirements, so none are declared here. Ownership and agreement are pending human review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity this person record belongs to; business key of the Person asset and a reference to BusinessEntity.

schema.name: PersonType
schema.description: Code classifying the type of person (for example, employee, customer, or contact). Allowed values are not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: NameStyle
schema.description: Flag indicating how the name is written/ordered (e.g., standard vs. eastern order).

schema.name: Title
schema.description: Courtesy title of the person (e.g., Mr., Ms.).

schema.name: FirstName
schema.description: Given name of the person.

schema.name: MiddleName
schema.description: Middle name or initial of the person, if any.

schema.name: LastName
schema.description: Family name (surname) of the person.

schema.name: Suffix
schema.description: Name suffix of the person (e.g., Jr., Sr.), if any.

schema.name: EmailPromotion
schema.description: Code indicating the person's email promotion preference. Allowed values are not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: AdditionalContactInfo
schema.description: Additional contact information for the person, stored as semi-structured (XML-like) content.

schema.name: Demographics
schema.description: Demographic survey information about the person, stored as semi-structured (XML-like) content.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the source row, used for replication.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: PersonPhone
contracts.doc: Staging asset for person phone numbers from the source PersonPhone table. Each record links a person (by BusinessEntityID) to a phone number and its phone number type. The contract enforces the declared schema, business-key uniqueness and not-null rules (handled by the deterministic core); no value-level thresholds are stated in the requirements, so ownership and further semantics are left to human review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the person (business entity) that the phone number belongs to; references the Person/BusinessEntity record.

schema.name: PhoneNumber
schema.description: The telephone number of the person, as recorded in the source system.

schema.name: PhoneNumberTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the phone number type (e.g. as defined in PhoneNumberType) classifying this phone number.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time when the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: PhoneNumberType
contracts.doc: Reference data describing the types of phone numbers (e.g. cell, home, work) that can be associated with a person's phone number. Sourced from the PhoneNumberType source table and staged as-is; the contract enforces the declared schema and key integrity. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: PhoneNumberTypeID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the phone number type; referenced by PersonPhone.PhoneNumberTypeID.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the phone number type, e.g. the kind of phone (cell, home, work).

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source system.

contracts.name: StateProvince
contracts.doc: State or province reference records from the source Person schema, staged one row per StateProvince. The contract enforces the declared schema and key constraints; value-level semantics are left for producer/consumer negotiation and human review.

schema.name: StateProvinceID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the state or province record.

schema.name: StateProvinceCode
schema.description: Code identifying the state or province (ISO-style abbreviation).

schema.name: CountryRegionCode
schema.description: Code of the country or region the state or province belongs to; references CountryRegion.

schema.name: IsOnlyStateProvinceFlag
schema.description: Flag indicating whether the record is the only state/province for its country or region (i.e. StateProvinceCode is not used).

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the state or province.

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales territory the state or province belongs to.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the source row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

# Generated Data Vault project (vault-agent)

A runnable dbt project: `models/staging/` computes the hash keys / hashdiffs via
AutomateDV's `stage` macro, `models/raw_vault/` holds the generated hubs, links, and
satellites. Review `review-queue.md` and `contracts/` before agreeing the model.

## Provide the raw inputs

Each staging model reads one raw relation by name — provide it either as a dbt seed
(`seeds/<name>.csv`, headers exactly as listed) or as a table/view in the target schema:

- `BusinessEntity` → feeds `stg_business_entity_businessentity` (expected columns: BUSINESSENTITYID, MODIFIEDDATE, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `Person` → feeds `stg_business_entity_person` (expected columns: BUSINESSENTITYID, PERSONTYPE, NAMESTYLE, TITLE, FIRSTNAME, MIDDLENAME, LASTNAME, SUFFIX, MODIFIEDDATE, EMAILPROMOTION, ADDITIONALCONTACTINFO, DEMOGRAPHICS, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `EmailAddress` → feeds `stg_business_entity_emailaddress` (expected columns: BUSINESSENTITYID, EMAILADDRESS, MODIFIEDDATE, EMAILADDRESSID, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `PersonPhone` → feeds `stg_business_entity_personphone` (expected columns: BUSINESSENTITYID, MODIFIEDDATE, PHONENUMBERTYPEID, PHONENUMBER, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `Password` → feeds `stg_business_entity_password` (expected columns: BUSINESSENTITYID, MODIFIEDDATE, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `Address` → feeds `stg_address` (expected columns: ADDRESSID, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `AddressType` → feeds `stg_address_type` (expected columns: NAME, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `ContactType` → feeds `stg_contact_type` (expected columns: NAME, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `PhoneNumberType` → feeds `stg_phone_number_type` (expected columns: PHONENUMBERTYPEID, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-11-15
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 115 requirement(s) and 18 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (7)

- **hub_business_entity** — business key `BusinessEntityID`. Company-wide party register (customers, vendors, employees, persons); persons share the same party number and are not a separate hub. Email, phone and credential relations are registered as feeds since they carry the same party number. Integrated from 5 source(s): BusinessEntity.BusinessEntityID, Person.BusinessEntityID, EmailAddress.BusinessEntityID, PersonPhone.BusinessEntityID, Password.BusinessEntityID; canonical staging key column `BUSINESSENTITYID`. _(requirements: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-065)_
- **hub_address** — business key `AddressID`. Postal address identified by its own address number, shareable across parties. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-007-2)_
- **hub_address_type** — business key `Name`. Address type reference (Billing, Home, Shipping), keyed on name per decided key. _(requirements: REQ-011-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-056)_
- **hub_contact_type** — business key `Name`. Contact type reference describing the role a person plays for an organisation, keyed on name per decided key. _(requirements: REQ-035-2, REQ-036-2, REQ-056)_
- **hub_phone_number_type** — business key `PhoneNumberTypeID`. Phone number type reference (home, work, mobile). _(requirements: REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-045, REQ-056)_
- **hub_country_region** — business key `CountryRegionCode`. Country or region identified by ISO code. _(requirements: REQ-020-2, REQ-056)_
- **hub_state_province** — business key `Name`. State or province reference, keyed on name per decided key. _(requirements: REQ-021-2, REQ-056)_

### Links (4)

- **link_address_state_province** — connects hub_address, hub_state_province. The state or province in which an address sits (country derived via state). Unit of work: AddressID + StateProvince. _(requirements: REQ-002-2, REQ-003-2, REQ-005-2)_
- **link_state_province_country_region** — connects hub_state_province, hub_country_region. Every state or province belongs to exactly one country or region. Unit of work: StateProvince + CountryRegionCode. _(requirements: REQ-022-2, REQ-023-2, REQ-003-2)_
- **link_business_entity_address** — connects hub_business_entity, hub_address, hub_address_type. Party-address relationship qualified by address type; party, address and type together are unique. Unit of work: BusinessEntityID + AddressID + AddressType. _(requirements: REQ-009-2, REQ-010-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-015-2, REQ-016-2, REQ-018-2)_
- **link_business_entity_contact** — connects hub_business_entity, hub_business_entity (person), hub_contact_type. Organisational contact relationship: organisation party, person party acting as contact, and contact role. Unit of work: BusinessEntityID (organisation) + PersonID + ContactType. _(requirements: REQ-033-2, REQ-034-2, REQ-035-2, REQ-037-2, REQ-038-2, REQ-039-2, REQ-040-2, REQ-042-2, REQ-043-2)_

### Satellites (17)

- **sat_business_entity_details** — on hub_business_entity; payload: ModifiedDate. Business entity register last-changed timestamp; rowguid excluded as technical metadata. Source table: BusinessEntity. _(requirements: REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008)_
- **sat_business_entity_person_name** — on hub_business_entity; payload: PersonType, NameStyle, Title, FirstName, MiddleName, LastName, Suffix, ModifiedDate. Person type and name details with history. Source table: Person. Split rationale: Ordinary name/type reporting data; carries the Person last-modified timestamp.. _(requirements: REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-032, REQ-049-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_person_consent** — on hub_business_entity; payload: EmailPromotion. Email promotion consent with full history. Source table: Person. Split rationale: Compliance-sensitive consent split out for audit history and access control.. _(requirements: REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-027, REQ-062, REQ-063)_
- **sat_business_entity_person_sensitive** — on hub_business_entity; payload: AdditionalContactInfo, Demographics. Sensitive XML additional contact info and demographics. Source table: Person. Split rationale: Sensitive classification and XML data type; restricted separately.. _(requirements: REQ-028, REQ-029, REQ-030, REQ-031, REQ-058)_
- **sat_business_entity_email** — on hub_business_entity; payload: EmailAddress, ModifiedDate. All email addresses of a person, numbered within the person, with history. Multi-active satellite, child dependent key: EmailAddressID. Source table: EmailAddress. _(requirements: REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-035, REQ-036, REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-049-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_phone** — on hub_business_entity; payload: ModifiedDate. All telephone numbers of a person qualified by phone number type, with history. Multi-active satellite, child dependent key: PhoneNumberTypeID, PhoneNumber. Source table: PersonPhone. _(requirements: REQ-039, REQ-040, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-049-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_credential** — on hub_business_entity; payload: ModifiedDate. Existence and last-change of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt excluded. Source table: Password. Split rationale: Separate source; credential values never loaded.. _(requirements: REQ-046, REQ-047, REQ-048, REQ-050, REQ-061)_
- **sat_address_details** — on hub_address; payload: AddressLine1, AddressLine2, City, PostalCode, ModifiedDate. Street address details with history. Source table: Address. _(requirements: REQ-002-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-006-2, REQ-008-2, REQ-049-2)_
- **sat_address_location** — on hub_address; payload: SpatialLocation. Geographic coordinates of an address. Source table: Address. Split rationale: Personal geographic data and spatial data type.. _(requirements: REQ-004-2, REQ-054, REQ-058)_
- **sat_address_type_details** — on hub_address_type; payload: AddressTypeID, ModifiedDate. Address type source identifier and last change. Source table: AddressType. _(requirements: REQ-014-2)_
- **sat_contact_type_details** — on hub_contact_type; payload: ContactTypeID, ModifiedDate. Contact type source identifier and last change. Source table: ContactType. _(requirements: REQ-036-2)_
- **sat_phone_number_type_details** — on hub_phone_number_type; payload: Name, ModifiedDate. Phone number type name with history of renames. Source table: PhoneNumberType. _(requirements: REQ-041, REQ-045)_
- **sat_country_region_details** — on hub_country_region; payload: Name, ModifiedDate. Country or region name with visible renames. Source table: CountryRegion. _(requirements: REQ-020-2, REQ-031-2, REQ-032-2)_
- **sat_state_province_details** — on hub_state_province; payload: StateProvinceID, StateProvinceCode, IsOnlyStateProvinceFlag, ModifiedDate. State or province code, no-genuine-code flag and identifier. Source table: StateProvince. _(requirements: REQ-021-2, REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-031-2, REQ-055)_
- **sat_state_province_territory** — on hub_state_province; payload: TerritoryID. Sales territory assignment of a state or province, tracked over time; territory descriptions come from the sales area. Source table: StateProvince. Split rationale: Territory assignment changes independently and needs its own history.. _(requirements: REQ-026-2, REQ-027-2, REQ-028-2, REQ-029-2, REQ-030-2, REQ-049-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_address_details** — on link_business_entity_address; payload: ModifiedDate. Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship. Source table: BusinessEntityAddress. _(requirements: REQ-017-2, REQ-018-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_contact_details** — on link_business_entity_contact; payload: ModifiedDate. Last-changed timestamp of the contact relationship. Source table: BusinessEntityContact. _(requirements: REQ-041-2, REQ-042-2)_

### Hub keys decided before modelling (4)

- **AddressType** — key `Name`: the declared natural key, taken as the default of a contested case; the requirements' first choice was `AddressTypeID` (0.60); primary key `AddressTypeID`.
- **ContactType** — key `Name`: the declared natural key, taken as the default of a contested case; the requirements' first choice was `ContactTypeID` (0.60); primary key `ContactTypeID`.
- **CountryRegion** — key `CountryRegionCode`: the requirements name it and the catalogue declares it unique; the requirements' first choice was `CountryRegionCode` (0.90); primary key `CountryRegionCode`.
- **StateProvince** — key `Name`: the declared natural key, taken as the default of a contested case; the requirements' first choice was `StateProvinceID` (0.75); primary key `StateProvinceID`.

### Source mappings (40)
